headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict exposure; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; plano can emit content through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and logs/metrics. A shared local filesystem or copy-paste bridge lets attacker-controlled content from either agent be treated as instructions by the other. This is plausible in default pair use, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF Cursor reads plano-generated text from a shared workspace or clipboard as instructions
IF plano forwards attacker-controlled prompts or tool outputs into Cursor-visible files
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Use separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit human review before copying agent output into prompts
Strip instructions from any shared files before opening them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can write files; plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml while using broad network egress. If they share a workspace or operator clipboard, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Cursor into plano’s networked context or logs. The pairwise leakage path is credible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local filesystem
IF Cursor content is copied into plano inputs or logs
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Avoid pasting secrets into either agent
Redact logs before sharing them
Restrict plano to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; plano also has broad network egress and can read config.yaml. Cursor’s shared_state_with_other_instances is via local filesystem, so concurrent instances can collide on the same mutable files and git state. The pair can therefore race on shared resources with irreversible repo damage.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or config directory
IF Cursor Yolo mode or shell actions modify git state while plano also writes shared files
mitigations: Run the agents on separate clones
Pause one agent before the other writes
Protect git branches with review-only merges
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, facts, and file edits; plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and routing/gateway behavior, so it may consume upstream outputs as authoritative. If plano forwards Cursor-produced text without verification, errors can cascade into downstream responses or actions. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show autonomous destructive actions by plano.
conditions: IF plano uses Cursor output as trusted input without validation
IF Cursor-generated code or claims are routed onward by plano
mitigations: Insert a verification step before forwarding outputs
Mark Cursor outputs as untrusted by default
Limit plano to summarization rather than action-taking
Sample-check forwarded facts against source files
requires-engineering: add schema validation for routed content

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and handles source code, open files, and optional model-provider API keys; plano is open-source and touches logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml. The profiles do not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch, but shared handling of logs and code can create policy gaps if sensitive data is routed into plano’s networked path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared logs or traces
IF organizational policy forbids code or secrets leaving the local workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared logs
Review retention settings for both tools
Use separate environments for sensitive projects
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
